title: Storage contract
description: The shape of a versioned table contract under contracts/storage/. A meta-schema, not a table definition: it constrains how ticks.v1.json and bars.v1.json are written so that the shared test fixture, the destructive-migration check, and a non-Python implementation can all read them without guessing. The tables themselves are created only by their owning service's migrations.

schema_version.description: Incremented in the same change as any column addition. Each table has its own lineage: the two tables have independent owners and release cadences, so their versions do not move together.

owner.description: The sole writer of this table's rows and of its DDL. No other service, and no platform bootstrap step, creates or alters it.

hypertable.description: The TimescaleDB time dimension. Every unique index on the table must contain this column.

type.description: A PostgreSQL type. Prices are double precision and timestamps are timestamptz; no column is JSONB, so every field stays visible to information_schema and to per-column compression.

nullable.description: A column added in a later version of this lineage must be nullable or carry a default, so a reader built against an earlier version keeps working.

default.description: A SQL default expression. A column added in a later version of this lineage must be nullable or carry one of these, so a reader built against an earlier version keeps working; the additive-only check enforces exactly that pair.

wire_field.description: The field of the corresponding wire record this column stores. Present on every column that has one, which is what lets a test hold the two contract surfaces together.

primary_key.description: Null where the table has none: on a hypertable a primary key must contain the partitioning column, which is not always the key the domain wants.
